events.title: Proximity Exhibition

venue.name: Snug Harbor Cultural Center
venue.address: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C)

events.description: Discover PROXIMITY, featuring 10 Snug Harbor studio artists across painting, photography & mixed media. Explore how shared spaces and creative con
events.details: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor's longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place-it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another. events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located in Tottenville on Staten Island
events.details: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies. Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp's great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance. It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. Public Garden Walks are most appropriate for adults or young adults. Not intended for groups; groups should sign-up for Private Garden Tours . Severe weather cancels. Registration not required for this drop-in event. Questions? Please email us at information@wavehill.org or call 718.549.3200 x251. events.title: Meet the Artists: Dots and Loops
events.description: Join us for a series of participatory events and workshops with exhibiting artists.
events.details: Join us for a series of participatory events and workshops with exhibiting artists Jen Chen-Su Huang, Rita Maas, and Audra Wolowiec, whose work is display in the Wave Hill House exhibition Dots and Loops. Dots and Loops presents works that respond to the idea of language as score, exploring its relationship to the natural world through metaphor and meditation. This Meet the Artist event will blend performance, textile-making, and meditative drawing, as each artist conducts a hands-on activity based on their respective artistic practices. Meet the Artist is an ongoing series of conversations between exhibiting artists, the curatorial team, and sometimes invited guests at Wave Hill. The program offers visitors, the artists' community, and others an opportunity to hear from the artist and gain deeper insight into their work.

events.title: Wayne Tucker and the Bad Mothas - Tribute to Marshal and Ernie Royal
events.description: Enjoy a free concert at Oak Ridge!
events.details: Wayne Tucker is a New York-based trumpeter, vocalist, composer, and bandleader whose work blends jazz, soul, gospel, funk, R&B, and singer-songwriter traditions. He has performed and recorded with artists including Taylor Swift, Jay-Z, the Roots, Elvis Costello, and Jon Batiste while leading his own group, Wayne Tucker and The Bad Mothas. \"I think my music is 100% vulnerable,\" Tucker says. \"I'm unafraid to express that true uniqueness.\" Tucker will present his original music and also perform music by Marshal and Ernie Royal of Ozone Park Queens. 2:30pm Doors, 3pm Concert This event is sonsored by Councilmember Joann Ariola and The Forest Park Trust.
